name: The Laboratory of the Mind
description: The chasm between the humanities and the sciences that C.P. Snow documented in The Two Cultures might be bridged by considering a technique shared by humanists and scientists: the thought experiment. Reasoning from imaginary cases is common to almost every field of human inquiry. Some scientists are every bit as imaginative as poets; and some poets construct arguments as rigorous and exacting as those produced by a geometer. More puzzling than the fact that poets, physicists and lawyers are united in using thought experiments is the fundamental challenge of thought experimentation generally
